data.one_liner: A simple yet powerful state management technique for Flutter with zero boilerplate.
data.what_it_does: Provides an integrated approach to state management, dependency injection, and navigation using reactive state injection. Handles asynchronous status automatically and supports state persistence and undo/redo.
use_when: You want state management with zero boilerplate and no code generation
You need built-in dependency injection, routing, and state persistence
You want simple handling of asynchronous futures and streams without manual tracking variables
avoid_when: You prefer the explicit event-to-state mapping of BLoC
You want to use Riverpod or Provider ecosystem instead
strengths: Zero boilerplate with no code generation required
Comprehensive feature set including dependency injection, navigation, and persistence
Built-in handling of asynchronous states (idle, waiting, error, data)
weaknesses: Less community adoption compared to Riverpod or Provider
Relies on a proprietary global/functional injection approach which can be unconventional
data.setup_notes: Add states_rebuilder to dependencies in pubspec.yaml

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a compile-safe, provider-based dependency and state management library.

alternatives.name: flutter_bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer strict event-driven architecture with predictable state transitions.

alternatives.name: provider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a lightweight, standard InheritedWidget wrapper for state propagation.
